A © B

')` returns `'A © B'`; `striptags('no tags here')` returns `'no tags here'`; `striptags('')` returns `''`.", "public_names": ["striptags"], "requires": [], "why_requires": ""}, {"id": "m2", "title": "Add run_postprocessors and render_inner_html; rewire TocTreeprocessor.run to strip footnote refs from heading content", "requests": ["R1", "R2", "R7"], "requirement": "Add public `run_postprocessors(md, text)` (applies every registered postprocessor in `md.postprocessors` to `text` and returns the result) and `render_inner_html(md, elem)` (returns the serialized inner HTML of an ElementTree element) to `markdown/extensions/toc.py`. Rewrite `TocTreeprocessor.run` so that heading content is processed through `run_postprocessors` followed by `striptags` (from m1) to produce the plain-text name, replacing the deprecated `get_name`/`stashedHTML2text` calls. Footnote reference superscripts must be absent from the TOC link text.", "observable": "`from markdown.extensions.toc import run_postprocessors, render_inner_html, striptags` all succeed. Converting `'# Header with footnote[^1]\\n\\n[^1]: text'` with `extensions=['toc','footnotes']` produces a TOC `` whose text is `'Header with footnote'` (no trailing `1`). `run_postprocessors(md, 'x')` returns text after md's postprocessors have run. `render_inner_html(md, elem)` returns a string of serialized inner markup. The existing tests testBaseLevel, testHeaderInlineMarkup, testHtmlEntities, testHtmlSpecialChars, testRawHtml still pass.", "public_names": ["run_postprocessors", "render_inner_html", "TocTreeprocessor.run", "striptags"], "requires": ["m1"], "why_requires": "TocTreeprocessor.run calls `striptags` (added in m1) to convert postprocessed heading HTML into plain-text name; without striptags defined in the module the run method raises NameError during conversion."}, {"id": "m3", "title": "Populate toc_tokens with name/html/data-toc-label; sanitize data-toc-label via striptags; call html.unescape only before slugify", "requests": ["R4", "R5", "R6"], "requirement": "Each entry in `md.toc_tokens` must contain keys `name` (plain text with entities preserved), `html` (rich rendered inner markup), and `data-toc-label` (the raw attribute string). The `data-toc-label` value must be sanitized through `striptags` (from m1) independently before being written into `name`, fixing a bug that allowed markup through. An `html.unescape` call must be made immediately before `slugify` so slugify operates on decoded Unicode, but `html.unescape` must NOT be applied to `name`, `html`, or `data-toc-label`.", "observable": "For heading `# Foo & Bar` with `{data-toc-label='Custom & Label'}` and `extensions=['toc','attr_list']`: `md.toc_tokens[0]['name']` equals `'Custom & Label'` (entities preserved), `md.toc_tokens[0]['data-toc-label']` equals `'Custom & Label'`, `md.toc_tokens[0]['html']` contains rendered markup with `&`, and the generated anchor `id` is `'custom-label'` (html.unescape turned `&` into `&` before slugify stripped it). The existing tests testHtmlEntities and testHtmlSpecialChars still pass.", "public_names": ["TocTreeprocessor.run", "toc_tokens", "striptags", "run_postprocessors", "render_inner_html"], "requires": ["m1", "m2"], "why_requires": "TocTreeprocessor.run calls `striptags` (from m1) to independently sanitize `data-toc-label` before writing it to `name`, and relies on the `run_postprocessors`+`striptags` pipeline wired up in m2 to produce the `name` and `html` token fields; without m1's `striptags` the separate sanitization raises NameError, and without m2's pipeline the token fields are never populated."}], "expected_causes": ["striptags might accidentally call html.unescape internally, violating the entity-preservation requirement and breaking testHtmlEntities.", "run_postprocessors might not iterate all registered postprocessors in correct order or might fail on AtomicString inputs returned by earlier processors.", "Footnote-ref stripping might only handle the default `[^N]` pattern and miss edge cases like multiple refs or nested footnote syntax in one heading.", "html.unescape might be erroneously applied to name/html/data-toc-label instead of only before slugify, altering the preserved-entity behavior and breaking testHtmlSpecialChars.", "data-toc-label sanitization might reuse the heading-content pipeline rather than running striptags independently, causing double-processing or allowing raw markup through.", "toc_tokens entries might omit one of the three required keys or store them under different names, breaking downstream consumers.", "render_inner_html might serialize the element including its tag rather than just inner content, producing malformed html fields."], "verifier_plan": "m1: Import striptags from markdown.extensions.toc; assert striptags('A & B') == 'A & B'; assert striptags('

X

') == 'X'; assert striptags('plain') == 'plain'; assert striptags('') == ''. m2: Import run_postprocessors, render_inner_html, striptags from markdown.extensions.toc (striptags import proves m1); build a Markdown instance with toc+footnotes extensions; convert '# H[^1]\\n\\n[^1]: f'; parse resulting HTML and assert the TOC text is 'H' with no trailing '1'; call run_postprocessors(md, 'test') and assert postprocessors were applied; call render_inner_html(md, some_elem) and assert it returns serialized inner HTML string. m3: Import striptags (proves m1); convert a heading with data-toc-label='Custom & Label' using toc+attr_list; inspect md.toc_tokens[0] and assert keys 'name','html','data-toc-label' exist; assert name=='Custom & Label'; assert data-toc-label=='Custom & Label'; assert the generated id contains 'custom-label' (entities were unescaped only for slugify); assert html field contains '&' (not unescaped). Also run existing test suite tests for testBaseLevel, testHeaderInlineMarkup, testHtmlEntities, testHtmlSpecialChars, testRawHtml to confirm no regressions."}

raw_message.reasoning:
The user wants me to plan milestones for a coding task in the Python Markdown library. Let me analyze the requests and code links to create a proper ordered series of milestones.

Looking at the requests:
- R1: All postprocessors are now run on heading content.
- R2: Footnote references are now stripped from heading content.
- R3: A more robust `striptags` is provided to convert headings to plain text. HTML entities are not unescaped.
- R4: The plain text `name`, rich `html`, and unescaped raw `data-toc-label` are saved to `toc_tokens`.
- R5: The value of `data-toc-label` is sanitized separate from heading content before being written to `name`.
- R6: An `html.unescape` call is made just prior to calling `slugify` so that `slugify` only operates on Unicode characters.
- R7: The functions `get_name` and `stashedHTML2text` defined in the `toc` extension are both deprecated. Instead, third party extensions should use some combination of the new functions `run_postprocessors`, `render_inner_html` and `striptags`.

Code links show:
- `unescape` is called by `get_name` in toc.py
- `get_name` is called by `TocTreeprocessor.run`
- `slugify` is called by `TocTreeprocessor.run`
- `stashedHTML2text` is called by `TocTreeprocessor.run`
- `unescape` is called by `TocTreeprocessor.run`
- `slugify` is called by `slugify_unicode`

The findings_to_address mention that the planned behaviour contradicts existing tests (testBaseLevel, testHeaderInlineMarkup, testHtmlEntities, testHtmlSpecialChars, testRawHtml). I need to plan requests compatible with existing tests.

Let me think about what the existing tests expect:
- testBaseLevel: Tests that TOC respects base_level config
- testHeaderInlineMarkup: Tests inline markup in headers
- testHtmlEntities: Tests HTML entities in headers
- testHtmlSpecialChars: Tests special characters in headers
- testRawHtml: Tests raw HTML in headers

These tests likely check that the TOC extension properly handles various content in headings. The key constraint is that `striptags` must NOT unescape HTML entities (R3), and `html.unescape` is only called before `slugify` (R6).

Let me design milestones:

**M1: Add `striptags` function** (R3)
- Public function `striptags(text)` in `markdown/extensions/toc.py`
- Strips HTML tags but preserves entities like `&`, `©`
- This is a foundation for everything else

**M2: Add `run_postprocessors` and `render_inner_html`, rewire TocTreeprocessor.run** (R1, R2, R7)
- `run_postprocessors(md, text)` applies all postprocessors
- `render_inner_html(md, elem)` serializes inner HTML of element
- TocTreeprocessor.run uses these + striptags instead of get_name/stashedHTML2text
- Footnote refs stripped from heading content
- Requires m1 because TocTreeprocessor.run calls striptags

**M3: Save name/html/data-toc-label to toc_tokens, sanitize data-toc-label, unescape before slugify** (R4, R5, R6)
- toc_tokens entries have `name`, `html`, `data-toc-label` keys
- data-toc-label sanitized through striptags separately
- html.unescape called only before slugify
- Requires m1 (striptags) and m2 (pipeline)

Let me verify the dependency chain:
- m1 is independent (foundation)
- m2 requires m1 (calls striptags)
- m3 requires m1 and m2 (uses striptags for sanitization, uses the pipeline from m2)

The code_links show:
- `get_name` calls `unescape` (both_mentioned: true)
- `TocTreeprocessor.run` calls `get_name`, `slugify`, `stashedHTML2text`, `unescape`

So the dependency is: TocTreeprocessor.run → get_name → unescape. The new design replaces get_name with striptags + run_postprocessors + render_inner_html pipeline.

Let me also consider R7 (deprecation of get_name and stashedHTML2text). This is part of m2 since it's about rewiring the pipeline.

Now let me think about what's compatible with existing tests. The tests check:
- HTML entities in headers should be preserved in the TOC display (testHtmlEntities)
- Special chars work (testHtmlSpecialChars)
- Raw HTML works (testRawHtml)
- Inline markup works (testHeaderInlineMarkup)
- Base level works (testBaseLevel)

The key insight from R3 is that `striptags` does NOT unescape entities. So `&` stays as `&` in the `name` field. But for slugify, R6 says `html.unescape` is called first, so `&` becomes `&` before slugify. This means the generated id would have `amp` or similar in it... wait, let me think more carefully.

Actually `html.unescape('&')` gives `'&'`, and then `slugify('Foo & Bar')` would give `'foo-bar'` (the `&` gets stripped). So the id is based on the unescaped text.

For the `name` field (plain text), entities are preserved: `'Foo & Bar'`.
For the `html` field (rich), the rendered markup is stored.
For `data-toc-label`, the raw attribute value is stored.

Let me finalize the plan.
